taskDescription: Drag the words into the correct boxes
resetDropDescription: Are you sure you want to reset this drop zone?
a11yCheck: Check the answers. The responses will be marked as correct, incorrect, or unanswered.
a11yShowSolution: Show the solution. The task will be marked with its correct solution.
a11yRetry: Retry the task. Reset all responses and start the task over again.
textField:
When your character needs to ask the player's name and remember it for later, you should store their answer inside a *variable*.
To make your sprite say "Hello" and the player's name in one single speech bubble, you must use the *join* block to glue the text pieces together.
Words or sentences that you type into your code, like "Game Over" or "You Win", are known as *strings*.
If you want your player to lose a life only when they touch a spike, you would place that rule inside an *if-then* block.
The computer uses *logic* to figure out whether conditions are currently true or false, such as checking if the game should continue.
To keep track of how many coins a player has collected, you must use *numbers* so the game can accurately add or subtract points.
We give our characters instructions by connecting different coding *blocks* together in the workspace to build a script.
